s: The Chola land tax of one-sixth of the produce was similar to the rate of which of the following?
x: The Chola rate of one-sixth matched the standard associated with the Pallavas and Kakatiyas. The Mughals and Sher Shah are associated with one-third, while the Gupta rate was about one-seventh.

s: Besides being landholders, employers and lenders, Chola temples were venues for the meetings of which body?
x: Chola temples were major landholders, employers and lenders, and also provided venues for village assembly meetings.

s: Which Chola ruler is associated with the title ‘Sungam Tavirtta Chola’?
x: Kulottunga I was called Sungam Tavirtta Chola, meaning the Chola who abolished tolls.

s: What did 'Kadamai' denote in Chola revenue terms?
x: Kadamai was land revenue in kind; Antarayam was the rural tax in cash.

s: Which of the following pairs (Chola revenue terms) is correctly matched?
x: Ayam meant royal dues; Irai was the tax on land, Kasu the gold coin and Eccoru the duty to feed visiting officials.

s: With which Chola ruler is the land survey of the Chola empire associated?
x: The Chola land survey was carried out by Rajaraja I.

s: What did 'Antarayam' denote in Chola revenue terms?

o: A very large village administered as a single unit
A village donated to a single Brahmin
A group of villages forming a nadu
Land set apart for the maintenance of the village tank

s: What were the colleges attached to temples in the Chola period called?

s: Which of the following South Indian states was famous for its naval power :
x: Chola Kings maintained massive consolidated troops with a proficient naval power. The Chola navy played a vital role in the expansion of the Chola Empire including the conquests of Ceylon (Sri Lanka) islands and naval raids on Srivijaya, Sinhala and Maldives.

s: Why was Rajaraja I given the title 'Ulakalanada Perumal'?
o: the king who abolished hereditary officials
the ruler who measured the earth, like Vishnu’s three strides
the conqueror of the entire island of Sri Lanka
the patron who built all the major Chola temples

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Kaikkolar referred to royal infantry regiments. Velaikkarar were loyal bodyguard troops, Kadagams were military cantonments, and Eri variyam was a tank committee.

s: Who were the Velaikkarar in the Chola military system?
o: Cavalry units recruited from Sri Lanka
Loyal bodyguard troops sworn to die with the king
Provincial governors appointed from among princes

s: Which Chola ruler is credited with building the Chola navy?
x: Rajaraja I is credited with building the Chola navy. Rajendra I later expanded its operations significantly.

s: With which place is Kadaram, captured by Rajendra I's 1025 CE expedition against Srivijaya, identified?
x: Rajendra I's Srivijaya expedition took Kadaram (Kedah) in Malaya and parts of Sumatra.

s: What were the royal infantry regiments of the Chola army called?
x: Kaikkolar were the royal infantry regiments; Velaikkarar were bodyguards sworn to die with the king.

s: What were Chola military cantonments known as?
x: Kadagams were cantonments; ghatikas were colleges and kottams/valanadus administrative units.

s: The Chola navy made which water body a 'Chola Lake', in the words of K.A. Nilakanta Sastri?
x: Nilakanta Sastri said the Chola navy made the Bay of Bengal a 'Chola Lake'.

s: Where did Rajaraja I's navy destroy the Chera navy?
x: Rajaraja I, who built the Chola navy, destroyed the Chera navy at Trivandrum.

s: Which committee was responsible for managing village tanks and distributing water to fields?
x: The eri variyam was the tank committee responsible for managing tanks and distributing water to fields.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Tank irrigation was a major feature of the Cholas' agricultural economy.
Kallanai was built by Karikala Chola.
Tank irrigation was unknown under the Vijayanagara rulers.
The Kakatiyas built large irrigation tanks.
x: Option C is incorrect: the Vijayanagara rulers built many tanks and reservoirs, such as the Porumamilla tank. Chola tank irrigation, Karikala's Kallanai and the large Kakatiya tanks are all correct.

s: Rajaraja I made the sabhas of Cholamandalam serve which temple?
x: Rajaraja I made the Cholamandalam sabhas serve the Brihadeeswara temple, showing the temple's role in administration.

s: Who built the Kallanai (Grand Anicut) on the Kaveri?
x: The Kallanai was built by Karikala; later Cholas kept up the delta channels.

s: Which statement about Chola inscriptions is correct?
o: They were confined to military victories and contain no economic information.
They are mostly brief records written only in Sanskrit and unrelated to administration.
They were written primarily in Prakrit because Tamil was not used administratively.
They are among the most voluminous and detailed sources from South India, with Tamil as the language of administration.
x: Chola inscriptions are the most voluminous and detailed in South India, and Tamil was the language of administration.

s: With which of the following are the Tiruvalangadu copper plates mainly associated?
o: The genealogy and conquests of Rajendra I
The survey of land by Rajaraja I
The construction of the Grand Anicut by Karikala
The abolition of tolls by Kulottunga I
x: The Tiruvalangadu plates of Rajendra I provide Chola genealogy and accounts of conquests.

s: The Larger Leiden (Anaimangalam) plates record a grant to the Chulamanivarma-vihara built by the king of which kingdom?
x: The plates, ordered by Rajaraja I and engraved under Rajendra I, grant Anaimangalam village to the vihara built by the Srivijaya king Sri Mara Vijayotunga Varman; they use Sanskrit and Tamil.

s: The smaller Leiden plates associated with the Chudamani Vihara comprise:
o: 21 sheets and record the construction of the vihara by the Srivijaya king
21 sheets and record Rajaraja I’s original grant only
3 sheets and record Kulottunga I’s extension of the grant after an appeal by two Javanese envoys
3 sheets and record Rajendra I’s expedition to Kadaram

s: What were the Ashtadasha Tirthas in the Eastern Chalukya administration of Vengi?
x: The Ashtadasha Tirthas were the 18 departments; the Yuvaraja was a partner in governance and councils were called Varagoshti.

s: To the reign of which Chola ruler do the Anbil plates, with a Sanskrit genealogy, belong?
x: The Anbil plates are of Sundara Chola; the Tiruvalangadu plates are of Rajendra I.

s: In May 2026, which country returned the Leiden copper plates of the Cholas?
x: On 16 May 2026 the Netherlands returned the plates at The Hague, the first return of Chola copper plates.

s: What were the councils of the Eastern Chalukya administration called?
x: The Eastern Chalukyas had 18 departments (Ashtadasha Tirthas) and councils called Varagoshti.

x: Various trade unions existed in South Indian townships like Manigramam, Nanadesi, Valanjiyar, etc. The purpose of these unions was to encourage trade and business.

s:
Consider the following statements about merchant guilds of South India.

I. Ayyavole merchant guild was originally established in Aihole.

II. Manigraman merchant guild was sub-ordinated to the Anjuvannam merchnat guild in the 13th century.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
x: Statement I is correct: Ayyavole-500 originated from Aihole in Karnataka. Statement II is wrong: the notes describe Manigramam as a foreign/long-distance trade corporation, and nothing says it was subordinated to the Anjuvannam, a guild of West Asian merchants.

s: Which merchant guild originated from Aihole and operated pan-regionally and overseas?
x: Ayyavole-500 originated from Aihole; Manigramam was a foreign-trade corporation, Ubhaya Nanadesi handled domestic and foreign trade, and Nagaram was a market-town assembly.

s: Who headed the Nakaras (merchant bodies) under the Eastern Chalukyas?
x: Nakaras headed by Shreshthis traded under the Eastern Chalukyas, and Ayyavole and Manigramam were active in Andhra, especially around Penugonda.

s: What were the Ayyavole 500 and Manigramam of the Chola age?
x: Ayyavole 500 and Manigramam were merchant guilds of the Chola age, part of a sea trade running from Sri Lanka through Malaya and Sumatra to Southeast Asia.

s: What happened to the independence of the merchant guilds as Chola power declined?
x: Merchant guilds, which had emblems and militias, acted as bankers and donated to temples, became more independent as the Cholas declined.

s: Which merchant body of the Chola age handled both domestic and foreign trade?
x: Ubhaya Nanadesi engaged in both domestic and foreign trade; Nagaram was local and Nanadesi foreign.

s: What was 'Nagaram' (Nakaram) in the Chola age?
o: Local merchant assembly of a market town
x: Nagaram was the local merchant assembly of a market town; Manigramam and Nanadesi were foreign-trade bodies.

s: Whose guild was the Anjuvannam?
x: Anjuvannam was the guild of West Asian foreign merchants.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Chola merchant guilds?
o: They had their own symbols and militias.
They were confined to local trade alone.
x: Guilds such as Ayyavole-500 and Manigramam carried inter-regional and overseas trade; the other features are correct.

s: How many branches did the merchant guilds of Penugonda have across Vengi?
x: Penugonda was the main trade centre of medieval Andhra, where Ayyavole and Manigramam had 18 branches across Vengi.

s: Which place was a trade centre between Kalyan and Vengi?
x: Tagara was the trade centre on the route between Kalyan and Vengi; the others were ports.

s: Which merchant guilds were active at Penugonda, the main trade centre of medieval Andhra?
x: Ayyavole and Manigramam were active in Andhra, especially at Penugonda, with 18 branches across Vengi.

s: Which merchant guild's name meant 'of many countries' and dealt in foreign trade?
x: Nanadesi (also called Pekkundru) means 'of many countries' and was a foreign-trade guild.

s: The wider historical significance of the Chola merchant-guild networks was that they:
o: replaced all temple institutions with royal agencies
confined trade to inland Tamil markets
ended commercial contacts with China and Southeast Asia
carried Chola trade and Dravidian culture across the Bay of Bengal
x: The guild networks extended Chola commerce and Dravidian cultural influence across the Bay of Bengal.

s: In which year did Kulottunga I send 72 merchants to China?

s: Under which Chola ruler did relations with Srivijaya turn hostile over the China route?
x: Relations were friendly under Rajaraja I but turned hostile under Rajendra I, who sent the 1025 expedition.

s: Chola embassies of 1015 and 1033 reached the court of which Chinese dynasty?
x: Chola embassies reached the Song court in 1015 and 1033.

s: Where was the 1088 Tamil inscription of the Ayyavole-500 merchant guild found?
x: Barus (Lobu Tua) has the 1088 Ayyavole-500 inscription; Takua Pa names Manigramam and Pagan has a Nanadesi Vishnu temple inscription.

s: The Tamil inscription at Takua Pa in Thailand names which guild?
x: The Takua Pa inscription names Manigramam; Pagan in Myanmar has a Nanadesi Vishnu temple.

s: Which of the following pairs (guild record abroad – place) is correctly matched?
x: The Nanadesi Vishnu temple is at Pagan (Myanmar); the 1088 Ayyavole-500 inscription is at Barus and Takua Pa names Manigramam.

s: Which was the main port of the Cholas, where the Chudamani Vihara stood?
x: Nagapattinam was the main Chola port and site of the Chudamani Vihara.

s: In which of the following is Quilon (Kollam), a centre of Arab and Chinese trade, located?
x: Quilon is a Kerala port where Arab and Chinese traders came.

s: At the mouth of which river did Kaveripattinam (Puhar), the port of the Sangam Cholas, lie?
x: Kaveripattinam was the Sangam Chola port at the mouth of the Kaveri.

s: Which one of the following represents the correct classification of major exports and imports in Chola overseas trade?
o: Exports: horses and porcelain; Imports: textiles and pepper
Exports: textiles, pepper and precious stones; Imports: horses, Chinese silk, porcelain, camphor and aromatics
Exports: Chinese silk and horses; Imports: paddy and land grants
Exports: camphor and aromatics; Imports: spices and precious stones only
x: The principal exports included textiles, pepper and precious stones. Imports included horses, Chinese silk and porcelain, camphor and aromatics.

s: Which of the following was an import, not an export, in Chola overseas trade?
x: Horses were imported; textiles, pepper and precious stones were exported.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched in Chola overseas trade?
x: Pepper was an export; the other pairs are correct.

s: Which of the following did not form a part of the donations made to the temple?
The king of which kingdom built the Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam?
x: The Buddhist Chudamani Vihara was built by the Srivijaya king Sri Mara Vijayottunga Varman.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Chola temple economy:
1. Temple income came from guild donations and royal grants of land and paddy.
2. Rajaraja I granted the village of Anaimangalam to the Chudamani Vihara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: temples drew on guild donations and royal grants, and the Larger Leiden plates record Rajaraja I's grant of Anaimangalam.

s: Which Srivijaya king built the Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam in 1006?
x: Sri Mara Vijayottunga Varman built the Chudamani Vihara in 1006; Rajaraja I granted it Anaimangalam.

s: Which was the central location of the trade centre in medieval Andhra?
x:
Penugonda was one of the most important commercial centres of medieval Andhra. It occupied a strategic position connecting the coastal ports with the inland regions. The town was famous for merchant guilds such as the Ayyavole-500 and Manigramam, which carried on extensive inland and overseas trade. It also emerged as an important centre of the Komati merchant community. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).

• Medieval Trade Centre – Penugonda
• Famous Merchant Guilds – Ayyavole & Manigramam

s: The Nagara style of temple architecture emerged prominently in which region and period?
o: The Deccan from about the 8th century CE
North India from about the 5th century CE
South India from about the 3rd century CE
Eastern India from about the 10th century CE
x: The Nagara style is associated with North India and is identified from about the 5th century CE.

s: Which dynasty started the Vesara style of temple architecture?
x: Vesara, blending Dravida vimana tiers with the Nagara curvilinear profile, was pioneered by the Badami Chalukyas; the Hoysalas came later.

s: With which of the following is the Nagara style of temple architecture associated?
x: The Nagara temple has a curvilinear shikhara, while the Dravida temple has a pyramidal vimana and elaborate prakara walls and gateways.

s: Chola temples represent the zenith of which temple style?
x: Chola free-standing structural temples are the zenith of the Dravida style, not Nagara; the style continued under the Kalyani Chalukyas and Hoysalas.

s: What is the topmost, dome-like crowning part of the vimana called?
x: Shikhara denotes the topmost, dome-like crowning portion of the vimana; the monolithic shikhara of the Thanjavur temple is especially noted.

s: Which one of the following correctly explains the term ‘Garbhagriha’ in Dravida temple architecture?
o: The womb-house containing the principal icon
The pillared hall used for gatherings
The raised platform of the temple
x: Garbhagriha literally denotes the womb-house and houses the principal deity or icon of the temple.

s: What is the 'antarala' in temple architecture?
o: vestibule between the sanctum and the mandapa
x: The antarala is the vestibule between sanctum and mandapa; the mandapa is a pillared hall, the jagati a raised platform and the gopuram the entrance gateway.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the comparative development of Dravidian art?
o: The Pallavas laid its foundation and the Cholas developed it on a monumental scale.
The Cholas laid its foundation and the Pallavas built its monumental culmination.
The Rashtrakutas alone created the Dravidian tradition.
The Hoysalas laid its foundation and the Kakatiyas completed it.
x: The comparison states that the Pallavas laid the foundation of Dravidian art, while the Cholas built its monumental culmination.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Khajuraho temples are in the Nagara style. Kailasanathar is Rajasimha style, the Mahabalipuram Rathas are Mamalla style and Chausath Yogini is circular.

s: The Draksharama Bhimeswara temple in Andhra Pradesh is built in which style?
x: Draksharama Bhimeswara is in the Chalukya-Chola style; Padmakshi at Hanamkonda is Kakatiya.

s: What is the pillared hall of a Dravida temple called?
x: The mandapa is the pillared hall; antarala is the vestibule, jagati the platform and prakara the enclosure walls.

s: What does 'prakara' refer to in temple architecture?
x: Prakara means the enclosure walls; the raised platform is the jagati.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
x: Option C is incorrect: the Dilwara Jain temples are at Mount Abu in Rajasthan, while Morena is known for the circular Chausath Yogini temple. Jagannath–Puri, Virupaksha–Hampi and Konark–Odisha are right.

s: What is the name of the many-storeyed entrance gateway of a Dravida temple?
x: The gopuram is the many-storeyed entrance gateway; the vimana is the tower over the sanctum.

s: What is the pyramidal tower over the garbhagriha of a Dravida temple called?
x: In the Dravida style the vimana is the pyramidal tower over the garbhagriha (sanctum).

s: Which of the following temples has a Dravida-style pinnacle with Nagara-style ornament?
x: The Teli temple at Gwalior has a Dravida pinnacle with Nagara ornament; the other three are Nagara temples.

s: Who founded the Jagannath temple at Puri?
x: The Jagannath temple at Puri was founded by Anantavarman Chodaganga of the Eastern Gangas.

s: In which style is the Kailasanathar temple at Kanchi built?
x: The Kailasanathar temple at Kanchi is in the Rajasimha style of Narasimhavarman II; the Mahabalipuram Rathas are Mamalla style.

s: The Kapoteswara temple, first Buddhist and later Shaiva, is located at which place in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Kapoteswara temple at Chejarla was a Buddhist shrine later turned Shaiva.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Padmakshi temple at Hanamkonda is a Kakatiya temple, not Pallava.

s: The Dashavatara temple at Devgarh belongs to which period?
x: The Dashavatara temple at Devgarh is a Gupta temple, not a Chandela temple of Khajuraho.

s: Which one of the following statements about Brihadeswara Temple at Tanjavur is not correct?
o: The temple is a splendid example of Chola architecture.
It was built by Emperor Rajaraja I.
The temple is constructed of granite.
